acceptedAnswer.text: csslib is a home for free, open-source CSS projects. Each project is independent: use the visual studios in Atelier, drop Vektor.css into a page, or take just the parts you need.
Yes. Every project is released under the MIT License, with no sign-up and no paid tier.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a build step or framework?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The studios run in your browser and export plain CSS, and the libraries are single stylesheets you link from any page.
More studios, libraries and experiments built on modern native CSS. Follow along on GitHub.

pages.title: Kinetix Studio — Free CSS animation generator | Atelier by csslib
pages.description: Choreograph responsive CSS animations on a visual node graph. Kinetix Studio turns CSS keyframe animation into a flowchart you can see. Chain steps, run them in parallel, route different motion to different screen widths, and export production-ready @keyframes with the media queries already written.

pages.title: ChromaFlow — Free CSS gradient generator | Atelier by csslib
pages.description: Paint rich mesh-style gradients with perceptual OKLCH colour. ChromaFlow lets you paint a background instead of describing it. Drop colour emitters on a canvas, shape how far each one reaches, and export gradients that blend in OKLCH, so colours stay vivid instead of turning muddy grey.

pages.title: Specimen Lab — Free CSS property playground | Atelier by csslib
pages.description: Put any visual CSS property under the microscope. Specimen Lab is a hands-on playground for 32 visual CSS properties. Drag handles right on the stage, read how the browser really computes each value, and copy the exact declaration when it looks right.

pages.description: Build responsive page layouts that adapt without media queries. IntrinsicFlow builds page structure visually. Arrange semantic regions, give each one an intrinsic behaviour such as an auto-fit grid or a sidebar switcher, pin headers and sidebars, and export clean HTML and CSS.
